newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica slams firm aiding Papua New Guinea army.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica slams firm aiding Papua New Guinea army.

text.p: South Africa's Foreign Ministry said on Monday it was "dismayed" that mercenary firm Executive Outcomes would help the Papua New Guinea government in its nine-year fight against seccessionist rebels.
The firm said last month it would provide consultancy assistance, aircraft, equipment and specialist training to Papua New Guinea armed forces.
"The Department of Foreign Affairs expresses its dismay regarding the involvement of a South African based para-military group...in the conflict," the ministry said in a statement.

Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan has confirmed that his government has hired mercenaries as advisers to accompany local troops on a mission against the Bougainville Revolutionary Army (BRA).

Executive Outcomes, Africa's best known private army, which has helped Angola and Sierra Leone fight rebels, said it had been sub-contracted by British-based military consultancy Sandline International that was recently awarded a contract in the South Pacific country.

"Executive Outcomes has been sub-contracted to train the Papua New Guinea security forces as part of the many faceted strategy to reach a lasting solution to the nine year-old crisis in Bougainville," the group said last month.
